question.text: The derivatives trading platform used by NSE is called:

answer.text: NEAT-F&O (National Exchange for Automated Trading - Futures & Options)

explanation.text: The Logic: NSE uses the NEAT (National Exchange for Automated Trading) system. The derivatives segment uses NEAT-F&O specifically. It is a fully automated screen-based trading system that enables members to enter orders from their terminals. The Trap: BOLT is BSE's trading system. ODIN is a third-party trading front-end software. CTCL is a facility for connectivity, not a trading platform itself. Cross-Exam Context: Exchange infrastructure knowledge is tested across multiple NISM modules. Distributor's Pro-Tip: NSE uses NEAT-F&O for derivatives trading - a fully automated, screen-based, anonymous order-driven system.
